request.deadline: Three-month liquidity deployment after enactment with monthly reporting; administrator confirmation expected within 30 days of enactment.
deliverables: Shared BTC reserve architecture with reserve-ratio mechanics and safety zones
Composable Cardano-native FIRE and ICE assets
Open-source SDKs and adapters for wallets, DEXs, and DeFi protocols
Always-on public dashboards for reserve ratio, asset supply, liquidity health, fee flows, and deployment status
Monthly governance reports and reporting standards
Independent security review, audit, and economic modeling
Legal/compliance disclosures, treasury reporting, risk documentation, and launch-readiness review
request.recipient: Sundial Protocol and Charms, with Intersect proposed as interim fund administrator subject to confirmation and final agreement.
request.what: Fund Alchemy, a Cardano-native Bitcoin treasury protocol and BTCfi infrastructure layer by Sundial Protocol and Charms, including reserve architecture, FIRE and ICE assets, dashboards, adapters, reporting, audits, administration, legal/compliance work, go-to-market execution, and staged launch liquidity.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 10,000,000 ada, using an approximate USD 0.20 per ada reference value for an approximately USD 2.0 million planning budget split into two approximately USD 1.0 million pools.

Pool 1 is intended for protocol infrastructure and staged launch liquidity, kept separate from operating expenses, deployed over three months, and structured so profits, yield, and returns from the launch liquidity position are returned to the Cardano Treasury quarterly.

Pool 2 is intended for delivery, audits, integrations, dashboards, governance reporting, legal/compliance work, and go-to-market execution with itemized planning allocations totaling approximately USD 1.0 million.

Alchemy proposes a shared BTC reserve architecture where FIRE and ICE are backed by the same BTC reserve, with reserve ratio formula (V x P) / L, FIRE price formula ((V x P) - L) / N+, an initial 5.0x reserve-ratio target, and safety zones above 4.0x, between 2.0x and 4.0x, and below 2.0x.

FIRE is described as a volatility-absorbing residual claim on the BTC reserve after ICE commitments, while ICE is described as a USD-denominated BTC-backed asset designed for lower-volatility exposure with growth potential.

The proposal asserts that Cardano currently lacks serious production BTCfi infrastructure and that without Alchemy, Bitcoin-backed structured exposure will continue consolidating on other chains and off-chain capital markets.

The proposal cites Strategy Q1 2026 results, Strategy Bitcoin holdings figures, Strive BTC accumulation, and on-chain products such as Apyx, Saturn, and Pendle as evidence that demand for Bitcoin-backed structured exposure is meaningful and growing.

The proposal acknowledges BTC volatility, oracle, bridge, Charms protocol-layer, novel asset, delivery, and adoption risks, and proposes mitigations including overcollateralization, safety zones, independent review, economic modeling, staged deployment, dashboards, legal/compliance work, milestone gating, fund separation, reporting, administrator oversight, and pause rules.

Intersect is proposed as interim fund administrator, subject to confirmation and final agreement, with an alternative independent administrator to be nominated if Intersect does not confirm within 30 days of enactment.

The proposal states that administrator-held ada will be kept in auditable accounts and delegated to auto-abstain rather than to a Stake Pool Operator, and that unused delivery funds, price-protection excess ada, and launch-liquidity profits, yield, and returns will be returned to the Treasury under the reporting process.

summary: The document requests 10,000,000 ada for a Cardano BTCfi infrastructure and launch-liquidity package, with detailed budget pools, reserve mechanics, reporting, risk mitigations, and administrator controls, while several market-size and strategic-gap claims remain partly proposer asserted or externally checkable rather than proven inside the document.
